newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish shepherds try to shoo bear back to France.
newsitem.headline: Spanish shepherds try to shoo bear back to France.

text.p: Shepherds in Spain's northeastern region are trying to frighten a bear back to France because they believe it has taken a liking to their flocks.
The farmers have blown horns, shot into the air and used powerful spotlights day and night to try to shoo Giva the bear back into the French Pyrenees, a Barcelona newspaper reported on Friday.

Giva, one of three Slovenian bears released into the mountains to boost a virtually extinct bear population, is believed to have eaten eight sheep in 12 days after straying into a farming region, La Vanguardia said.
Furious farmers in the Catalan sheep farming district just south of the Pyrenees have also set up electric fences around their flocks to deter the six-year-old bear.

Their actions angered ecologists, who say Giva is naturally very shy and easily disturbed by noise. They find it curious that Giva would have such an appetite as such bears normally eat berries and fish in the summer.

"The solution to this chaotic and desperate situation that the farmers are facing lies in the hands of France or ultimately with the European Union which financed the Life (bear reintroduction) programme," said Carles Barrera, chairman of the Valley Hunters' Society.
